Given this stuff is potential ice-9 style end of the world I think protocols should be a little stricter.

Maybe something about all samples taken must be recorded and held in designated storage, all personnel must go through full decontamination showers/clothes change and thoroughly searched before leaving the site etc.
The Foundation definitely does not want even a milligram of this stuff getting into the outside world either accidentally or by sabotage.

Also maybe there should be some at least a proposal to start trying to melt this thing down. A huge job for sure, but the Foundation has extreme resources and it is a potential XK after all.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Even if it doesn't reflect IR, it's not stated to actually be transparent to it, and both it and the air around it are cooler than ambient temperature. That said, it should be made clear in the article whether 630 and 630-1 are opaque or transparent - if they're opaque, then they'd still be visible, just totally black.

In response to Tom90deg below, I'm assuming that the emergency containment protocol would basically entail surrounding 630 with normal water ice, which appears to be unaffected by it. I do agree that the ambiguity about whether 630's meltwater is normal or not could stand to be addressed.

My own little quibble - I honestly think it's slightly less effective that once 630-1 freeze up, they turn into pure ice. Removing that note would leave the possibility that there's something or someone frozen into the main glacier somewhere. Mysteries like "is someone or something inside there", "what is it", and "why is it there" can be very nice to have in an SCP article.

Upvoted in spite of the quibbles, because I love the concept.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Intresting idea, a little vague, but not bad, seems to add to it. Reminds me of Ice-9 a bit. I was a bit confused by the possible "Emergency Cryogenic Containment Protocol" use. If it's for people, then they'll just be effected, but if it's for items, seems that a container of liquid nitrogen would be more effective.

Also, Some of the descriptions seems a bit wordy, the line about needing a "sustained exothermic chemical reaction of significant temperature" to melt the ice stuck out the most. Does it need to be a chemical reaction? Will a blowtorch work? Also, what happens to the melted substance? does it turn to water, or instantly re-freeze as soon as the heat is removed?

All in all, an interesting idea, I'll be keeping an eye on it.
